title: Problems connecting to multiple PX4s in SITL
author: varunvp
body:
I want to write a DroneCore program to control a swarm of SITL PX4s simultaneously, through offboard mode. Right now, I'm using a swarm of 4 drones, which is a modification of the scripts here:https://dev.px4.io/en/simulation/multi-vehicle-simulation.html. I've been using the takeoff_land example program from DroneCore as a base, When I run the example program, the first drone with a sysid of 1 takes off, which is as expected. Now if I have to control all the 4 drones, I have to add the 4 UDP ports of the drones, which I did, as below.

```
DroneCore::ConnectionResult connection_result = dc.add_udp_connection(14540);
dc.add_udp_connection(14541);
dc.add_udp_connection(14542);
dc.add_udp_connection(14543);
```

Of all these, I just want to add device for one drone, for the sake of testing. 
` Device &device = dc.device(1/2/3/4(mavlink sys ids));`
Now here comes the problem. It seems that all the PX4 SITL drones have the same UUID, so even differentiating between the MAVLink sys id 's is useless, because DroneCore won't even consider them. So I had to comment out this part of code from device_impl.cpp, so that it forces use of sys id.

```
// if (_target_uuid == 0 && autopilot_version.uid != 0) {

// // This is the best case. The device has a UUID and we were able to get it.
// _target_uuid = autopilot_version.uid;

// }
```

Even after doing all this, I start getting the following stream of errors, when I use any sys id other than 1 to connect.

title: mavsdk_server doesn't check if the server it is connected to is MavSDK.
author: AlexisTM
body:
## Problem:

If another gRPC server is already on port `50051`, MavSDK connect function succeeds, while the mavsdk_server starts and silently fails in the background.

For us it was `QIKService3`, some Qualcomm service for board discovery, which was listening on `tcp6://0.0.0.0:50051`.

Ideally, there should be a verification the server we connected to is valid.  

## To reproduce

Instal `QIKService3` or a gRPC test server on 50051.
I tried netcat listening on port 50051 without success, so I suppose  it probably needs to be a gRPC server.

```python
import asyncio
import logging
import sys
from mavsdk import System

logging.basicConfig(stream=sys.stdout, level=logging.DEBUG)

drone = System()
await drone.connect(system_address="udp://10.151.60.12:14550")
# This succeeds even if no drone is connected because a server listen on 50051
version = await drone.info.get_version()
# This causes an error because get_version is not implemented.
# mavsdk_server dies silently in the background 
```

## Log

By default, the logging does not report those errors.

```
>>> drone = System()
>>> await drone.connect(system_address="udp://10.151.60.12:14550")

Would it, though? If `mavsdk_server` starts successfully, then you will eventually receive MAVLink messages (that's your system identification). If `mavsdk_server` fails, you won't receive any MAVLink, but your gRPC "identification" call will fail just the same.

As you say, `mavsdk_server` knows that the port is already bound, and fails:

```
DEBUG:mavsdk.system:[01:07:14|Error] Failed to bind server to port 50051 (grpc_server.cpp:172)
DEBUG:mavsdk.system:Failed to start, exiting...
```

So to me, your problem here seems to be that somehow you did not have access to the `mavsdk_server` logs. Any kind of automation we would put on top of this would result in you getting the error message where you want it (because if the port you want to use for `mavsdk_server` is already bound, there is no way it will ever work).

Maybe my question would be: why did it take a long time for you to access the `mavsdk_server` logs, and do you think there is something that could make it easier? My feeling is that it is a bit of a leaky abstraction: users have to understand that there is a server running under the hood, so that if it doesn't work they immediately go check its logs :thinking:.

What do you think? :innocent:

> If connect() would check that mavsdk_server was successfully running and throw an exception otherwise instead of continuing as if everything is fine, that would solve the issue here I believe.

How would `connect()` make the difference between `UNIMPLEMENTED` and "mavsdk_server has stopped"? Or between "mavsdk_server has stopped" and "mavsdk_server did not start (e.g. the executable was not here)"?

> Yet another option would be to check the port before launching mavsdk_server and warn or throw an exception if it is not free.

Hmm it feels like a hack to me :sweat_smile:. But nothing prevents you from doing it from your code, before you start MAVSDK!

> Another option that would help is if we can promote mavsdk_server errors to loglevel error instead of debug.

Maybe there is something to do there, though I assume that users may end up turning the MAVSDK logs off (the issue here exists because at least you guys don't keep them enabled all the time, so it seems like a fair assumption :grin:).

Maybe there is something to do with the return code of `mavsdk_server`? Like MAVSDK-Python could detect that `mavsdk_server` stopped (with or without an error code) and... I don't know... throw an exception in Python? But then again, the exception would say "something wrong happened with `mavsdk_server`, please check the logs" :see_no_evil:.

I would be happy to see a good solution to that, but I guess my conclusion is that I don't see one myself :innocent:. Open to your suggestions of course!

> Yes, logging if the process exits before we expect it to would be a step in the right direction and most likely sufficient. Do you have any objections to this solution?

No, I think it would make sense for MAVSDK-Python to monitor `mavsdk_server` when it runs it :+1:.

My personal opinion is that by trying to always automate all use-cases, we make everything more complicated and we never address all use-cases.

I see MAVSDK-Python running mavsdk_server on 50051 by default as a "quick convenience" when we want to test something in the REPL. But for a production app, I would always have my application run mavsdk_server itself and connect MAVSDK-Python to it. That way my application can run mavsdk_server on an ephemeral port (possibly multiple instances of MAVSDK-Python).

@dakejahl is this still an issue? Did you ever encounter it again? I still have not been able to replicate it.

I haven't dug into it anymore. My changes should not affect this code path in particular. I suspect it's probably an architecture specific issue (Zero W is ARMv6 and the compiler is arm-linux-gnueabihf-g++)

If you have a Zero W on hand you can try that example I posted above, here's my docker file too for reference

**Dockerfile**
```
FROM dockcross/linux-armv6

ENV DEFAULT_DOCKCROSS_IMAGE my_cool_image

RUN wget http://sourceforge.net/projects/boost/files/boost/1.58.0/boost_1_58_0.tar.bz2/download && \
	mv download boost.tar.bz2 && \
	tar xjvf boost.tar.bz2 && \
	cd boost_1_58_0/ && \
	echo "using gcc : arm : arm-linux-gnueabihf-g++ ;" >> project-config.jam && \
	./bootstrap.sh --show-libraries && \
	sudo ./bjam --with-filesystem link=static install -j10 && \
	cd /usr/local/lib && sudo rm libcurl.* && \
	cd /usr/local/include/ && sudo rm -rf curl/
```

You already know this but to use it...
```
docker build -t my_cool_image .
docker run my_cool_image > raspberry-armv6-container
chmod +x raspberry-armv6-container
sudo mv raspberry-armv6-container /usr/bin
```
Aha, that's a good point about RPi Zero. I can give that a try. Thx for the note.
Just to follow up. I did try this on a RPi Zero against a board with ArduPilot flashed, and I could not reproduce it.
Closing, please re-open if it still happens and if you can give me instructions how to reproduce it, thanks.

verified.note: Maintainer could never reproduce it and closed asking for repro info that never came -- no working fix was ever confirmed.

title: seg fault when trying to read results of mavsdk::Param::get_all_params
author: weagle08
body:
MAVSDK version v1.4.4
PX4 v12.3

When I execute a get_all_params against the mavsdk::Param plugin I am getting a seg fault on a different thread immediately after trying to access any of the vectors of the mavsdk::Param::AllParams returned value. I'm doing the request after successfully connecting to a PX4 flight controller. I'm new to MAVSDK and mavlink in general so any assistance in tracking this down would be appreciated.

If i remove the timeout guard in mavlink_parameters.cpp line 821 the issue does not appear, but I don't think I want to remove this guard and have a potentially orphaned thread.
I noticed there were commits in this area on main so I tested against main as well and the problem still exists.

Possible culprit?

https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/7ebcc681eaf425c5426d12bc53b529bb90062f5c/src/mavsdk/core/mavlink_parameters.cpp#L994

instead of passing back a copy of the _all_params list, the actual list is returned and so when I access it on a different thread I think this is where the seg fault happens?

Amazing, thank you for the example! I'll try to tackle it this week.

I think the line you mentioned is not great indeed but I don't think that's the reason because in https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/v1.4/src/mavsdk/plugins/param/param_impl.cpp#L68 it creates a copy.

The error looks like a double fulfillment of a promise on `receive_timeout`. I thought I had fixed that one before :thinking:.

These:
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/1788/commits/812fa0a94c9871b1e032cdb3c35cd1bb8ead08bf
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/1788/commits/5ce3a5c2c821e5273c09a56ecf719eb5b36d52df

Now here comes the funny part. I just tried your example and couldn't reproduce it. I assume it depends on the PX4 version as well. I tested against PX4 `main`. I'll get back to this later.

Yes, you're right. It's definitely caused by double fulfillment of the timeout callback. That is odd that you could not reproduce the issue. I've only tested against PX4 running in a docker container. I'll try against actual hardware (CUBE H7 Blue) as soon as I can and post the result).

I also tried against PX4 SITL v1.12.3 and it works just fine.

My best guess is that you link against some MAVSDK .so file on your system that you're not aware of. It might be worthwhile to remove anything installed system-wide in `/usr` and `/usr/local`:

```
sudo apt remove libmavsdk-dev
sudo rm -rf /usr/local/include/mavsdk /usr/local/lib/libmavsdk.so /usr/local/lib/libmavsdk.so.* /usr/local/lib/cmake/MAVSDK
```

I do not utilize a locally installed version of MAVSDK. I build in the same manner as the project I posted, so it does a full build of mavsdk and links against the static lib that gets output. I'll keep looking at this as I'm very curious how the callback is even being hit twice because I see the lock guards and the checks for callback being null. Will report anything I find, but may be a couple weeks.

I'm going to close this since I seem to be the only one that's had this issue. I haven't had a chance to address it since using a passthrough subscription for params is fine for what I'm doing for now. and if it's a non-issue I don't want it sitting open. If someone else sees the problem they'll open a new issue I'm sure.

title: Changing mode to GUIDED
author: ygratz
body:
Hi,
I ran the takeoff_and_land example.
In some cases it did not takeoff. Now, I figured out that this was because the arducopter wasn't in GUIDED mode.
What can be the easiest way to command it to GUIDED mode ? 
At what class (Action, System,  ?) is that implemented.
Thanks

answer_comments.body:
[Here is](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/src/mavsdk/plugins/action/action_impl.cpp#L387) the ardupilot implementation of the takeoff. My understanding is that if it is not in GUIDED mode (which MAVSDK calls "offboard"), then it should set it to GUIDED and then takeoff.

Which version of MAVSDK are you using?

Oh, it is fixed in the main branch (which will become MAVSDK v2 at some point), but not in the v1.4.13 branch (which is the latest release): https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/v1.4.13/src/mavsdk/plugins/action/action_impl.cpp.

So you have two solutions:
1. Build MAVSDK from source from the main branch, so that you get the fix
2. Open a PR backporting the fix from main to the v1.4 branch, and then we could make a v1.4.14 release

I don't know how many similar fixes are in `main` and not in `v1.4` (apparently `v1.4` is currently 438 commits behind `main`: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/tree/v1.4). If I was using Ardupilot, I would personally build MAVSDK from source to make sure I don't miss other similar fixes.

But that's your choice :blush:.

Hello, I know this issue is closed but I'd like to add to it and perhaps suggest that it is reopened... I have changed to main branch, built from source etc. and the `takeoff` MavSDK action does work now... sometimes. I have been using the ArduPilot SITL environment to test my code and have noticed that I sometimes get a seg fault when using the `takeoff` command. I have tried out quite a few things and I *think* I have boiled it down to the `takeoff` command switching to `GUIDED` mode when there is no `position` as outlined in the logs shown in the image below. Based on [action.h](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/48f1ad0325ecdcb8075d7ffd0cd7a8323af12fb3/src/mavsdk/plugins/action/include/plugins/action/action.h#L84), I am getting a takeoff response of 13 which relates to `Failed` as shown below: ```cpp enum class Result { Unknown, /**< @brief Unknown result. */ Success, /**< @brief Request was successful. */ NoSystem, /**< @brief No system is connected. */ ConnectionError, /**< @brief Connection error. */ Busy, /**< @brief Vehicle is busy. */ CommandDenied, /**< @brief Command refused by vehicle. */ CommandDeniedLandedStateUnknown, /**< @brief Command refused because landed state is unknown. */ CommandDeniedNotLanded, /**< @brief Command refused because vehicle not landed. */ Timeout, /**< @brief Request timed out. */ VtolTransitionSupportUnknown, /**< @brief Hybrid/VTOL transition support is unknown. */ NoVtolTransitionSupport, /**< @brief Vehicle does not support hybrid/VTOL transitions. */ ParameterError, /**< @brief Error getting or setting parameter. */ Unsupported, /**< @brief Action not supported. */ Failed, /**< @brief Action failed. */ }; ``` I have also noticed that if I let the simulator "settle" for some time, I don't get this seg fault, presumably because there is a position. I have tested this on a real drone as well and have a similar issue, though I cannot simply let the drone settle as real GPS dropout causes a loss of position at any arbitrary time. In any case, I am unable to catch this error so it pretty much breaks my code, though I also need it for a drone takeoff. Thanks for your help!

Hi Oliver, thanks for reporting the issue. Could you maybe try by changing the takeoff code in your local MAVSDK to switch to Stabilize flight mode instead of guided mode before takeoff? Please check it on SITL ;) Relevant code is here.

https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/48f1ad0325ecdcb8075d7ffd0cd7a8323af12fb3/src/mavsdk/plugins/action/action_impl.cpp#L387

Stabilize mode does not need position so should not create this particular issue:
https://ardupilot.org/copter/docs/stabilize-mode.html#stabilize-mode

What is your use-case? You would need position fix anyways before carrying out an auto mission right? In such a case waiting for a good fix before activating takeoff should be prudent. Or are you flying indoors?

Arducopter allows to takeoff in a selected number of flight modes out of which Guided was selected since MAVSDK is supposed to control the drone from such a mode. But I am open to discussing this further to find the best suitable mode for takeoff for most scenarios. Would also discuss this with the ArduPilot Dev team shortly.

verified.note: Closed without confirmation from the original reporter, and a follow-up user shows the underlying takeoff/GUIDED-mode segfault is still unresolved on ArduPilot SITL.

title: mission_raw->mission_changed not received on mission clear all
author: Jonsen94
body:
If a mission is deleted from the drone no mission_changed event is triggered if it's deleted using the MAV_MISSION_TYPE_ALL-type. As can be seen in [0] the MAV_MISSION_TYPE type is checked. If it is MAV_MISSION_TYPE_ALL no mission_changed event will be triggered despite the mission changed (was deleted).

[0] https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/2e95299c656b06a46cc9594b71a169cb6095f985/src/plugins/mission_raw/mission_raw_impl.cpp#L63-L65

answer_comments.body:
Can you describe your setup? Is it something like below?

* PX4 running on the drone
* QGC running on the laptop, on udp://:14550
* MAVSDK running on the laptop, on udp://:14540

Can you reproduce the bug with SITL?

> QGC seems to upload missions with mission type 2 (MAV_MISSION_TYPE_RALLY) which also does not trigger a mission changed event.

This would be expected, because rally points are not technically mission items. And they are not supported with MAVSDK yet, I think.

It is called MAV_MISSION_ because it re-uses the mission messages for upload. But the "MISSION_TYPE" is RALLY.

I would say it's the correct implementation but we should add a `rally_points_changed()` notification for rally points.

I'm closing this because I think this would need to be fixed as part of a rally points plugin. To me it has not much to do with the mission_raw plugin which only handles MAV_MISSION_TYPE_MISSION for now.

@Jonsen94 feel free to start a PR in https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Proto if you want to add a rally plugin.

title: Add MAVSDK to Vcpkg
author: edalm
body:
[Vcpkg](https://github.com/Microsoft/vcpkg) is a package manager for C++ with many interesting features. It is based on CMake, supports multiple architectures, provides update mechanisms and integrates with any user project using CMake as its build manager.

Are there plans to add MAVSDK to Vcpkg? It would provide great benefits to developers using MAVSDK in their projects.

answer_comments.body: That would be a very good idea. I would have to read more about how it all works though. If you can give me pointers or instructions how to proceed that would be helpful.
Sounds nice! Wouldn't we need to check that our dependencies are available on Vcpkg, too? I guess we won't add a superbuild there, will we?

> EDIT: Therefore, MAVSDK wouldn't be responsible for building third_party libraries, as Vcpkg would do it automatically. These dependencies could then be linked using CMake's find_package().

That's already how MAVSDK works (i.e. all the dependencies are found with `find_package`). By default, we have `-DSUPERBUILD=ON`, which builds the dependencies at configure time and then sets `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` accordingly. But if you build with `-DSUPERBUILD=OFF`, it will get all the dependencies from your system.

So the way there would be to try to build with `-DSUPERBUILD=OFF` and to see if all of our dependencies are available in Vcpkg already. You can find them [here](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/tree/develop/third_party), but note that some of them are used for `mavsdk_server` (a.k.a. "backend") exclusively, as can be seen [here](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/develop/third_party/CMakeLists.txt#L19-L25). Which means:

Dependencies for MAVSDK-C++:
* jsoncpp
* tinyxml2
* zlib
* curl

Dependencies for `mavsdk_server`:
* All the dependencies of MAVSDK-C++
* libressl (or openssl or boringssl)
* cares
* protobuf
* absl
* grpc

I would start with MAVSDK-C++ (i.e. `-DBUILD_BACKEND=OFF -DSUPERBUILD=OFF`). @edalm can you check if Vcpkg has `jsoncpp`, `tinyxml2`, `zlib` and `curl`?

Awesome! I think you should try to go for it, then :slightly_smiling_face:. I would personally try to use Vcpkg to build MAVSDK first (as opposed to writing the portfile to make a package out of MAVSDK):

1. Clone MAVSDK
2. Setup your Vcpkg to get the dependencies (`jsoncpp`, `tinyxml2`, `zlib`, `curl`)
3. Build MAVDSK with the toolchain, as per your instructions above (don't forget to disable the superbuild). So something like:

```cmake
cmake -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=C:/vcpkg/scripts/buildsystems/vcpkg.cmake -DSUPERBUILD=OFF -Bbuild -S.
cmake --build build
```

If this builds, it means that MAVSDK was built using the dependencies from Vcpkg. Next step would then be to write the portfile to make a package out of MAVSDK, I guess.

comments.body: That would be a very good idea. I would have to read more about how it all works though. If you can give me pointers or instructions how to proceed that would be helpful.

Thank you for considering this suggestion.

**Vcpkg Overview**

Personally, I have been using Vcpkg for some time as an end user. I find it a very useful C++ package manager, which provides an easy mechanism to search, install and update libraries for any supported architecture. This is especially useful when developing on Windows, since libraries can be automatically downloaded, compiled and installed on a single directory, which can then be targeted with CMake rules.

In summary, Vcpkg downloads the library's source code from a public URL (e.g., GitHub repo), compiles the code for the chosen architecture, and installs the library on the predefined Vcpkg directory containing all installed libraries.

Then, developers who want to use these libraries in their projects only need to add Vcpkg's CMake toolchain by appending the following flag to CMake:
"-DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=C:/vcpkg/scripts/buildsystems/vcpkg.cmake"

**Contribute MAVSDK to Vcpkg**

Vcpkg's GitHub page contains instructions on how to add a new library to Vcpkg.
* https://github.com/microsoft/vcpkg/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#new-package-guidelines
* https://github.com/microsoft/vcpkg/tree/master/docs

Essentially, the project maintainer has to submit a PR on Vcpkg with the files required by Vcpkg. I have never submitted a project to Vcpkg, but from my understanding Vcpkg needs two mandatory files and optional patches.

The mandatory files are:
1. ```"CONTROL"```: with the library's information.
2. ```"portfile.cmake"``` with the rules on how to download, compile and install the library.

Optionally, patches may be provided in order to fix temporary issues either with Vcpkg or the project itself.

The list of libraries currently supported by Vcpkg are listed here:
https://github.com/microsoft/vcpkg/tree/master/ports
Sounds nice! Wouldn't we need to check that our dependencies are available on Vcpkg, too? I guess we won't add a superbuild there, will we?

The list of libraries currently supported in Vcpkg can be seen here (1000+):
https://github.com/microsoft/vcpkg/tree/master/ports

**Dependencies**

According to this [page](https://github.com/microsoft/vcpkg/blob/master/docs/maintainers/control-files.md), the dependencies of a given project should be listed in the ```CONTROL``` file, which has a syntax based on Debian's Control format. For instance, the curl library in Vcpkg depends on zlib. Thus, the curl's CONTROL file has the following line: ```Build-Depends: zlib```.

Regarding the dependencies of MAVSDK-C++, they are all supported in Vcpkg:

The instructions for building and installing MAVSDK should be declared in the ```portfile.cmake```.

title: Set rate position and attitude_euler not working with ArduPilot
author: julianoes

linked_prs.title: telemetry: Use REQUEST_DATA_STREAM for ArduPilot set_rate

comments.body:
Hello @julianoes ,
Is this issue open for contribution? I am a first-time contributor and would be happy to work on it if you could assign it to me.
@lakhmanisahil sure go ahead and make a pull request if you have a solution for it. I'm not working on it at the moment.
Thanks, @julianoes . I am looking into this issue and will aim to submit a PR.

Hi @julianoes, I've been studying the source (no hardware yet) and I think the fix should go inside `telemetry_impl.cpp`. All the `set_rate_xxx` functions call `_system_impl->set_msg_rate()` / `set_msg_rate_async()`, which internally send `MAV_CMD_SET_MESSAGE_INTERVAL` (cmd 511) — ArduPilot doesn't ACK this reliably on serial links. 

I can see `_system_impl->effective_autopilot()` is already used in `process_sys_status()`, so the fix would be to check `effective_autopilot() == Autopilot::ArduPilot` and fall back to `REQUEST_DATA_STREAM` instead for the affected rate setters. 

Planning to open a PR regarding this. Does that approach look right to you?

Files I'd change: [`telemetry_impl.cpp`](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/cpp/src/mavsdk/plugins/telemetry/telemetry_impl.cpp) · [`telemetry_impl.h`](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/cpp/src/mavsdk/plugins/telemetry/telemetry_impl.h)

Investigated the ArduPilot source — `MAV_CMD_SET_MESSAGE_INTERVAL` is fully supported for both `ATTITUDE` and `GLOBAL_POSITION_INT`. The command is correctly handled, ACKed, and applied.

The actual root cause is **GCS stream rate override**: when another GCS application (MAVProxy, QGC, Mission Planner) on the same MAVLink link sends `REQUEST_DATA_STREAM`, ArduPilot's `initialise_message_intervals_for_stream()` overwrites all individual message intervals in that stream group. So the rate set by MAVSDK gets silently clobbered.

Confirmed by ArduPilot issues: ArduPilot/ardupilot#17046, ArduPilot/ardupilot#19761, ArduPilot/ardupilot#28550.

**Workarounds:**
- Set `MAVn_OPTIONS` bit 2 (NOSTREAMOVERRIDE) on the ArduPilot port used by MAVSDK
- Ensure no other GCS sends `REQUEST_DATA_STREAM` on the same link
- When using SITL with MAVProxy, start with `--streamrate=-1`

This is not a MAVSDK bug — it's a user configuration issue on the ArduPilot side.
Oh, this makes more sense. Thanks for investigating @PavelGuzenfeld. I'll close this issue then.

title: Can the gRPC server be started before mavsdk-server discovers/connects to a system?
author: divyanshupundir
body:
In some cases, applications using mavsdk may start before the UAV system starts and is discovered by the mavsdk-server. In this case, clients intending to connect to the mavsdk-server will effectively have to block because the gRPC port will not be available.

Alternatively, if the gRPC server is up and the port is available, the clients won't have to block and the channels that are running in the background will automatically start receiving data once the UAV system is discovered.

The earlier versions of the mavsdk-server used to behave in the same manner which made client-side implementation quite easy.

answer_comments.body: Yeah it used to be that mavsdk would create a "dummy" system to receive subscriptions and whatnot, but that's not the case anymore. So your app has to wait until the drone is discovered before it can start the subscriptions. `mavsdk-server` is just reflecting that :innocent:

That won't work because the server implementation now needs to discover a drone. If you do that, your subscriptions won't ever have an effect because mavsdk won't save them for when a system is discovered.

Unfortunately I think that you have to deal with that on your side...

In my opinion, a very good next step for MAVSDK-Java would be to remove the dependency on gRPC and use direct bindings instead (i.e. JNI), so that it would be much more lightweight. But it also means that the API would get closer to the C++ API, which does not allow that at the moment.

And there you would see why this is problematic: MAVSDK-C++ supports discovering multiple drones, so if you subscribe to, say, the position updates before a drone is known, then MAVSDK cannot know if you were meaning to subscribe to the first or to the second drone that appears. That's why this is delegated to the user, because they know their use-case (and MAVSDK doesn't) :grin:.

title: Allow system-wide installation
author: julianoes
body: We should allow and support to install the library and headers into `/usr/local/`.

answer_comments.body:
@julianoes 
Thinking about this, linux/mac is definitely the main OS and system install is the desired pattern. We should aim to support that as the default.

The problems are that:
1. It doesn't work on windows
   * ... and there is no way to tell that as a user
   * therefore users have to use local install and we have to have complicated CMakeLists.txt files.
2. It breaks doc builds
   - is this because doxygen is looking in the wrong folder locations?
   - not that doc build doesn't work on windows anyway right now. 

So, suggestion:
1. Make system install the default
   - If someone does this build on windows fail and display a message "System install not supported on windows - do `THE COMMAND to build locally`
2. Make docs build against system install path (doxygen config file change). On Windows fail the docs call with a message that"Automated docs builds not supported on Windows".
3. Example code has to stay the same - that should build on windows too.
4. Docs change to separate out how you can point to local installs as a separate topic.
Thoughts?

title: Move deps like tinyxml and jsoncpp to plugins
author: devbharat
body:
Now that its possible to selectively enable/disable building plugins with the plugins.txt file, dependencies(like openssl, CURL, tinyxml and json) that are only needed by certain plugins can perhaps move to the needed plugin's own CMakeLists.txt file?

CMake also [allows that](https://stackoverflow.com/a/75246115). Perhaps this is too much of an optimization, but if someone just wants to use core library (and no plugins) downloading and installing these takes a bit of time and seems unnecessary.
resolution_evidence: thread converges on a working answer

answer_comments.body:
> If you are doing a local build and install of mavsdk with externalproject_add(), you’d need to clone & build for every fresh build

No you don't. Just:

1. Build the [third_party](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/tree/main/third_party) deps and install them somewhere (either by running from `./third_party` with `-DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/path/to/where/you/install/deps` or with the MAVSDK option [-DDEPS_INSTALL_PATH](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/CMakeLists.txt#L52) which does exactly that).
2. Then when building your project, add `/path/to/where/you/install/deps` to `-DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH`. Whether or not you install mavsdk with the deps or use `externalproject_add` doesn't matter, the MAVSDK CMakeLists will look into `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` at configure time.

That works when cross-compiling, too :+1:.

Dependency management is often over-estimated and wrapped into layers of tooling, I find. But it's pretty simple: you need your dependencies "installed" somewhere, and then you need to tell your build system where to find them. The build system looks on your system by default, but if you install them locally somewhere, you can tell your build system to look there (with CMake that's with `-DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH`).

I admit that the wrappers in MAVSDK are a bit convoluted (my bad :see_no_evil:), but now I do it [like this](https://www.acarg.ch/posts/cmake-deps/), if you are interested.
What about the find_package calls? Do you just move them to the plugins too?
@Consti10 I'd love a PR that removes the `std::filesystem` hack. I would be glad to have that gone.
jsoncpp as an example is used in core now anyway, so the discussion is moot.

comments.body: So, there is now an option to disable cURL. However, tinyxml2 and jsoncpp are going to get more important in many parts in a couple of component information features that are coming up, so I'm less motivated to move them.
Unless there is an actual use-case, I'd say we can keep it the way it is. We provide helpers to help build them, they can be linked statically, and they are really not big :+1:.

Makes sense. The use-case is rather straightforward, say you just want to use mavsdk passthrough plugin (say for integration testing of another code-base) you shouldn't need much.

Or perhaps you'd want to add your own plugins and build on top of the "core" mavsdk outside the mavsdk repo (not sure if we already can or if it needs a bit more modification to enable such 'external' plugins, need to check) after including it as a library in another project, it seems weird to have to install dependencies for plugins you are not even building. But i agree tinyxml and jsoncpp are not too much. Feel free to close!

What about the possibility to manually disable the dependencies like we did it for cURL?

I think that might be easier than having it flow out of the CMakeLists.txt configure step.

The problem I see is that if we move the `find_package` into the plugin's CMakeLists.txt then we also need to set some sort of variable to signal to third_party/CMakeLists.txt that it's not required. However, we run the third_party/CMakeLists.txt first, so we don't know yet at that time. And we have to run it first, otherwise the package won't be found later. :man_shrugging:
This reminds me that we should actually merge: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/1955.

My concern is that every such steps adds complexity for a specific use-case. Disabling curl is an answer to "what if I want only a subset of the camera plugin?". Now tinyxml and jsoncpp are for a subset of the other plugins. It's all adding branches in the build system and in the code that make it more convoluted.

My question would be: is this because people don't want to build the deps (curl admittedly takes quite some time to cross-compile), or is it because those deps don't build for their microcontroller?

title: Dynamic plug-in infrastructure
author: shakthi-prashanth-m
body:
DroneCore has its functionality built with compile-time plug-ins such as `Action`, `Mission`, `Telemetry`, etc. When DroneCore is built, we can choose which plug-ins we're interested in. Build chooses plug-ins in `plugins` directory and generates `DevicePluginContainer` class and methods to access to the "choosen" plug-in objects. It is necessary to build DroneCore if we wanted to add a new plug-in to it.

We're interested to add new plug-ins which DroneCore will pick it up run-time. Theoretical approach for this is [here](https://px4.slack.com/archives/C68J8H32A/p1506435370000733).

However, as we're interested to developing language bindings using gRPC; gRPC requires `.proto` files for each of the plug-in to be known at compile-time.
We're yet to investigate the feasibility of both (gRPC & dynamic plug-in). 

Updates on this activity will posted here.

answer_comments.body:
> Well, we can't have it all I think.

The whole problem to be addressed by this issue is summarised up the top as: "It is necessary to build DroneCore if we wanted to add a new plug-in to it."

That isn't sorted by this suggestion. So I'm not concerned about having it all, but the fact that we're talking about solutions that don't meet any stated requirement.

That isn't to say that this isn't a good idea, just that the reasons why it is a good idea have not been stated.

* When you start the connection with `udp://:14540`, it's equivalent to `udp://0.0.0.0:14540`, and it says "have MAVSDK _listen_ (/bind to) on 14540". In that mode, the drone must send MAVLink messages to MAVSDK on port 14540.
* When you start the connection with `udp://192.168.1.12:14555`, then it tells MAVSDK to start sending MAVLink heartbeats to the drone (here `192.168.1.12`) on port 14555. In that mode, the drone must listen (bind) to 14555.

Note that I invented the IPs and ports, you can use whatever you want. The point is just that `udp://:<port>` and `udp://0.0.0.0:<port>` run mavsdk in "server" mode, and `udp://<some_ip>:<port>` run mavsdk in "client" mode.

Does that help?

Oh... sorry I read too quickly :sweat_smile:. I don't know if it would make sense to add support for Iridium in MAVSDK, but could you make a bridge, say like this?

```
[------ on the ground -----]                                                [--- on the drone ---]
MAVSDK <--- udp ---> bridge     <------------ Iridium --------------->       drone
```

So you write your UDP-to-Iridium bridge on the ground, and connect MAVSDK to it over UDP. For MAVSDK, it's just a UDP connection, and the drone just receives MAVLink messages.

Then the question would be whether or not MAVSDK generates too much traffic for your connection, I guess?

Basically MAVSDK expects some heartbeats from the drone. Are you saying you would not have heartbeats? If so, we would have to make a config option that allows to have the timeout much bigger. 

However, you sorta need to discover a system initially, otherwise you don't know what the target system ID and target component ID to send a command to.

MAVSDK also does a bit of initial back and forth to get some basic information. We would have to have some "low bandwidth" mode to avoid all that but it would require some work.

It feels quite specific, I'm not sure if it would fit in MAVSDK. It sounds like you really need to control what goes out of MAVSDK, so anyway I would personally do that with a proxy. Still it may be worth using MAVSDK instead of re-implementing the protocols (e.g. mission transfer, commands, etc).

You can already increase the timeout for commands in MAVSDK. Then for the heartbeat, one way would be to have your proxy "pretend to be the drone" and send regular heartbeats to MAVSDK (say your proxy sends a heartbeat every second, and receives the heartbeats from the drone at whatever rate you want). title: UDP reconnect logic with PX4
author: al2950
body:
I think this issue has probably caught a few people out in the past. But when using UDP with PX4, PX4 will record the port & ip address of the first heartbeat it receives. It will then send any status and responses to this address. This address is set once, and only once, and so if you disconnect and reconnect with a different local port (on client), you will not receive any messages until the PX4 is rebooted.

Suggest adding a default port to MavSDK which it attempts to bind to, currently it is set to 0 so OS picks a 'sensible' random port.

comments.body: Isn't that a PX4 issue? If PX4 only supports one UDP client and needs to be rebooted to move to a new one, then it has to be fixed on the PX4 side, doesn't it?
One thing to note is that PX4 re-uses the same ports, so they are both set statically, while MAVSDK chooses the local port randomly.

> Isn't that a PX4 issue? If PX4 only supports one UDP client and needs to be rebooted to move to a new one, then it has to be fixed on the PX4 side, doesn't it?

Maybe, but I dont think its a bug in PX4.

Firstly (in PX4) most of the logic assumes a single client, allowing multiple clients would add complexity (which in turn decreases reliability)  Secondly adding logic to monitor a client, and potentially drop it if it does not hear from it may result in unintended dropped clients due to a network hitch... which would be a safety concern. 

I have not discussed this on the PX4 github, but my pov was that it would be way easier to just allow a user to specify a local port with MAVSDK. If not then i suggest adding this note to the troubleshooting docs

Disclaimer: I am not the one who needs to be convinced, I'll leave the final word to Julian 😇. But I'd like to share my opinion, which is that PX4 having to reboot in order to swap to a different client is a bug. And allowing to set the local port with MAVSDK would be a hack. The way I see client-server connections is that the server exposes a port and the client contacts it over this port. When I connect to GitHub, my browser does not set a local port to make it easier for GitHub to answer, and I don't need to reboot GitHub between two calls 🙈.

This said, without changing anything, I'm pretty sure that you can solve your problem with mavlink-router. Did you consider that?

I agree with @JonasVautherin but I'm also aware that we can't just change the way PX4 is set up, and we want to be compatible with it, so we should find a way.

@al2950 can you describe what steps I would take to reproduce this? I need to play with this to figure out exactly what is happening and then think through it.
I think I tried to fix this in PX4 a while ago: https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/pull/21608

> I agree with [@JonasVautherin](https://github.com/JonasVautherin) but I'm also aware that we can't just change the way PX4 is set up, and we want to be compatible with it, so we should find a way.
> 
> [@al2950](https://github.com/al2950) can you describe what steps I would take to reproduce this? I need to play with this to figure out exactly what is happening and then think through it.

Looking at [MissionItem](https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/develop/en/api_reference/classmavsdk_1_1_mission_item.html) it seems you are correct - it has gimbal yaw, but not vehicle yaw (which may differ).
@julianoes any reason not to support setting ROI too?

----

That said, this should not be "somewhat random". The way this works in MAVLink is that the [waypoint-like-items](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_NAV_WAYPOINT) have a yaw field. If the yaw is explicitly specified then that will be used. If the yaw is a NaN the vehicle will point towards whatever the system setting is (that is set using parameters, and default to "the next waypoint". 
The yaw can also be affected by the gimbal and ROI. 

If you were working in raw mavlink then I'd suggest calling the command to set an ROI. Not sure what to do now, but Julian probably will be!

I have many open question when it comes to ROI, modes of yaw during a mission, gimbal ROI, etc. To me it sounds like you need to be lucky in combining all these things to get it to work, and with MAVSDK we try to hide that sort of complexity and give you something (and sometimes only one thing) that works.
So yes it would be nice to support all this but we need understand all these aspects.

And you would like to be able to control both the yaw of the gimbal and the yaw of the drone, for some reason?

The gimbal yaw is not really used, we mostly need it for pitch changes and maybe roll later.
Our drone has other sensors and stuff pointing forward which are not on the gimbal. Instead of overloading the gimbal with too much stuff we find it a lot easier to control the drone yaw.
I could offset the gimbal so its facing the same thing as before but i have no idea what the drone yaw will be when reaching the waypoint so i can't give a good value when creating the mission item.

title: Maintain a connection instance per component in case of UDP
author: shakthi-prashanth-m
body:
Right now we've maintain one connection per System (one or more components).
This creates problem if there are more than one component in a system.

Consider below scenario:

- After we receive heartbeat from a component A of a system on udp port (say, 14540), we fill source ip/port details as part of connection instance. When we receive heartbeat from another component B of the same system, **_Core assumes System IP may be changed due to Wifi disconnection._**
- While we're sending commands/messages, we need to make sure we send to IP/Port of the corresponding component whom it is meant to be.

I think, to support multi-component in core, we shall have one connection per component. We should map each component with its connection to make this happen.

Please provide better suggestions, if any.
It is linked to #304 . And hopefully the fix should be part of #310 .

answer_comments.body:
Thanks @shakthi-prashanth-m. This is indeed something to think about. We're getting into the mavlink networking territory which is anything but trivial and not properly specced.

We can also have cases where there are two connections, one UDP (wifi) and one serial (a long range radio) to the same system possibly including more than one component.

The other question is if we should ever send commands to a specific component or if we can always send it on all connections and hope it will arrive in some way.

As we maintain only instance per connection, we keep overwriting onto it when received data from different components (same system or different).

I modified the issue to consider UDP connection only, because in case of UDP connection, we have chances of multiple components sending to a common port as below:

In absence of MAVLink Router these changes would be required. For now, we're closing this issue to keep DroneCore to have less complications. We may add it in future if required.

title: Add Functionality to Broadcast to Interface without Explicit Vehicle Connection
author: AlexKlimaj
body:
I am working on recreating the QGC RTK Base station functionality in a C++ application on a raspberry pi. I have the PX4 GPS driver running and now I am trying to figure out how to get mavsdk to broadcast the RTK corrections to all vehicles on two different interfaces. One serial and the other is UDP. 

It does not appear that mavsdk can do a broadcast to all connected vehicles. My approach is to discover all connected vehicles on the serial and UDP connections, then iterate through all of them doing a mavlink passthrough message to send the RTK corrections to each vehicle independently.

answer_comments.body: MAVSDK does not allow to broadcast messages right now. So right now it would just do the same loop as you do :+1:. I am not sure if broadcasting is in the scope of MAVSDK right now, because many things are not expecting to be broadcasted, right? Like all the commands, or basically any targeted message. Or is that incorrect?

I understand that broadcasting some messages may make sense (typically a GNSS base station wants to do just that). But at the MAVSDK level, the user does something like `drone.action.takeoff()`, where `drone` represents a MAVLink system (i.e. a pair of <sysid, compid>). Should MAVSDK allow for broadcasting the `takeoff` command? Because a command is a reliable message, MAVSDK expects to receive an ACK, otherwise it will resend the message. How do you broadcast a reliable message? How many ACKs do you expect, and from which <sysid, compid>? What do you do if one of them times out? Do you consider that your `takeoff` command failed? Or do you tell the user that it "partially succeeded"? Do you give a list of <sysid, compid>, with the result code for each of them?

I don't think it is trivial, but of course we are open to PRs if somebody figures out an nice API doing that in MAVSDK :blush:.
Maybe this is a hint that the MavlinkPassthrough plugin should not be a plugin but a direct API of the Mavsdk class. We could then add some sort of flag to signal the broadcast option.

You can now use the added [RawBytesConnection](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/2460e15689052b8cc3ce7fa4052bf584be0e7c83/src/mavsdk/core/include/mavsdk/mavsdk.h#L493-L528) and implement whatever sending/receiving protocol you want.

Personally, I'm not a fan of broadcast, so I'm not in favor of including it.

linked_issues.title: [Plugin] Forward RTK RTCM packets to FCU

comments.body:
Would you mind sharing which MAVLink messages are being sent for RTK? I think it may make sense to add them in MAVSDK (instead of having to use the passthrough).

> It does not appear that mavsdk can do a broadcast to all connected vehicles.

I would need more details about what you mean by "broadcast", because I find it generally ambiguous. Do you mean that you expect MAVSDK to send the message once over the air and have it reach all your vehicles, or do you want a helper such that you don't have to write a for loop to send the message once per discovered system?

This is the functionality in QGC.
https://github.com/mavlink/qgroundcontrol/blob/master/src/GPS/RTCM/RTCMMavlink.cc#L24

It is sending GPS_RTCM_DATA.
https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#GPS_RTCM_DATA

I think the broadcast of RTCM data in QGC is similar to how the heartbeat message is sent. A helper that could be called that you pass the RTCM data and the interfaces you want it broadcast over would be helpful. Maybe this doesn't align with mavsdk and I should just implement it using the c mavlink headers like QGC does.

I am not sure if broadcasting is in the scope of MAVSDK right now, because many things are not expecting to be broadcasted, right? Like all the commands, or basically any targeted message. Or is that incorrect?

I'm digging through QGC and it looks like it is also looking for vehicle heartbeats then sending targeted messages to them. So I'm not sure it is possible to broadcast to the entire network without knowing what the vehicle IP's are.

I understand that broadcasting some messages may make sense (typically a GNSS base station wants to do just that). But at the MAVSDK level, the user does something like `drone.action.takeoff()`, where `drone` represents a MAVLink system (i.e. a pair of <sysid, compid>). How do you broadcast a reliable message? How many ACKs do you expect, and from which <sysid, compid>? What do you do if one of them times out? Do you consider that your `takeoff` command failed? Or do you tell the user that it "partially succeeded"? Do you give a list of <sysid, compid>, with the result code for each of them?

I don't think it is trivial, but of course we are open to PRs if somebody figures out an nice API doing that in MAVSDK :blush:.
Maybe this is a hint that the MavlinkPassthrough plugin should not be a plugin but a direct API of the Mavsdk class. We could then add some sort of flag to signal the broadcast option.

You can now use the added [RawBytesConnection](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/2460e15689052b8cc3ce7fa4052bf584be0e7c83/src/mavsdk/core/include/mavsdk/mavsdk.h#L493-L528) and implement whatever sending/receiving protocol you want.

Personally, I'm not a fan of broadcast, so I'm not in favor of including it.

verified.note: maintainer explicitly declines the feature ('not in favor of including it'); OP worked around it outside MAVSDK -- this is a decline/wontfix, not a resolution

title: Link libc statically for Android
author: JonasVautherin
body:
From @Katawann on [discuss](https://discuss.px4.io/t/failed-to-run-mavsdk-server-in-react-native-app-on-android/20607):

### Context:
I’m trying to build an app on Android with React Native and using MAVSDK in it. It works like a charm if I run MAVSDK-Java client on the react app (on my device) and mavsdk_server running on a linux host. However my goal is to have both client and server on the app.

### Error:
When I add mavsdk_server in my app with implementation 'io.mavsdk:mavsdk-server:0.6.0', it fails with the following error:

```
More than one file was found with OS independent path 'lib/arm64-v8a/libc++_shared.so'. If you are using jniLibs and CMake IMPORTED targets, see https://developer.android.com/studio/preview/features#automatic_packaging_of_prebuilt_dependencies_used_by_cmake
```

### Root cause:
It seems that React Native already have a libc++_shared.so library and don’t know which one to load (supposition). I tried some solutions on React Native side but none of them work (same issue for other SDK that MAVSDK).

linked_issues.title: Link libc statically for Android
Missing filesystem symbols when linking libc on Android
React Native Module mavsdk-server

comments.body:
@Katawann: I think that you may be right in that MAVSDK-Java should not bring `libc++_shared.so` with it, and that's the reason for your issue. I do believe that the solution would be to build `libmavsdk_server.so` as a static library. We already do that for `mavsdk_server` (that we build as a static executable), so that should be similar (where instead of building a static executable `mavsdk_server`, for Android we want `libmavsdk_server.so` to link everything statically).

If you look e.g. [here](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/src/mavsdk_server/src/CMakeLists.txt#L102-L107), you'll find this `BUILD_STATIC_MAVSDK_SERVER` that we use in our CMakeLists.txt.

But [this is not done for Android or iOS](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/src/mavsdk_server/src/CMakeLists.txt#L92), where we only build `libmavsdk_server.so`. Maybe you could try to make it such that for Android, it does link statically into `libmavsdk_server.so`.

Does that make sense?
Closing due to inactivity. Feel free to reopen if necessary.

@JonasVautherin , I am facing the issue discussed https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Java/issues/65 while developing an application which requires NDK 21. I feel that the workaround for me as well is to build mavsdk_server as static library. Can you please guide me if it require changes to build or has already been done. Thanks a lot.

title: Simplify build process
author: dakejahl
body:
**Issue**
It's not super easy to build the library, and I'm not sure how to do a clean build without removing the dependencies added via FetchContent. It would be nice to be able to remove only the source build files so that we don't have to always redownload the dependencies (right now I just delete build/ and install/)

**Solution**
For my C++ projects I always add a Makefile to wrap the CMake commands. I like doing this because for every project I know I can run `make`, `make clean` and `make install`. The underlying actions of each recipe could vary, but it makes it easy for me to switch between projects without having to remember specifics of how they're built/deployed.

answer_comments.body:
> @JonasVautherin: Makefile wrapping CMake that PX4 used to have

Still has it, and I don't like it.

> @dakejahl: I shouldn't need to know all these details

I agree, except:
1. Dependencies are hard, and C++ doesn't have support for this, so it's up to the build system you choose or whatever else you do. We opted for cmake which means you need to learn/understand cmake. Yes, it's not just one command, but that's because we don't just support one OS or one setup.
2. And that is the second point. We could use something like vcpkg, conan, hunter, etc. and that might simplify things, however, as far as I'm aware that doesn't work for cross compilation builds that we support using dockcross, iOS, etc.. If we didn't have any cross-compilation it likely could be simpler.

> sane defaults that I can use for every project.

That's exactly what it would be: it would be defaults **for you** (and probably me) but not for everyone and so it can also create confusion. Having a `Makefile` would suddenly mean people will try to just use make, not realizing it's cmake, so I wouldn't want that. What I could see is a `build_linux.sh` sort of thing. However, you will end up adding arguments to this (MAVSDK bespoke) script that you will have to remember (e.g. build type). Over time you end up with this script encoding all sorts of cmake options, at which point we could just use [cmake-presets](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/manual/cmake-presets.7.html), and maybe that would be worthwhile. Last time I checked it wasn't quite supported for the cmake version we were targetting but by now it could be ok. I don't think I'd use it personally, mostly because it's yet another layer on top of cmake when I can just use the cmake configure lines that I have in my zsh history.

> @JonasVautherin I do that, too. That's why I want projects to use their tools in a standard way, so that I need to learn how to use Autotools, Meson, CMake, SwiftPkg, Carthage or Gradle only once, instead of having to learn a new build.sh for each project (which may call a Makefile wrapping CMake with custom functions that call Python scripts below).

That's exactly it. You put it better than I could @JonasVautherin.

> @dakejahl I don't want to learn anything, I don't want to read the docs

Sorry, you have to read the one page on how to build it, and take around 10s to type it out. I'm sorry we don't know how to make it simpler. (And no a git submodule mess is not going to happen.)

A dumb user should install the package from deb. A contributor needs to know the 3 arguments to cmake.

Here is another take on why I don't want a Makefile:

If I open the project in an IDE, say VSCode or CLion, I want it to detect that it's just cmake, and it will just work. If it also has a Makefile, it will ask you, and you need to know which one is the correct option. A developer new to it will be confused and not know which one to use.

And PX4 as an example: there is duplicated cmake logic in two places because of the "easy" Makefile:

1. https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/blob/4215e20120706221ce6f4cd0fab332a55f3bbeac/Makefile#L178-L196
2. https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/blob/4215e20120706221ce6f4cd0fab332a55f3bbeac/.vscode/cmake-variants.yaml#L4-L8
Fair enough. I understand where you're coming from and actually appreciate you bringing up friction points! This one is unfortunately one where it's not so easy, and we have opinions :).

> I thought if it's annoying for me it's probably annoying for others and thought it would be a good suggestion... wasn't trying to criticize or spark a debate.

And I didn't want to sound emotional or offended, sorry if that's how I came across :see_no_evil:. I guess my point is that I spent a lot of time trying different things and I haven't found a silver bullet :shrug:. Even modern language package managers come with their issues (often making it easier for developers but terrible for distro maintainers and security in general).

```cmake
cmake -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/path/to/where/you/want/third/parties -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/path/to/where/you/want/third/parties -Bbuild -S.

This should build and install the dependencies in `/path/to/where/you/want/third/parties`. This only needs to be done once. You may even skip that and install the dependencies from your system package manager if that works.

This is about proposal of **DroneCore shell**, a command line tool for interacting with a MAVLink device using DroneCore library. Its will be a handy tool for both users & developers.

$ dronecore action { arm | disarm | takeoff | land} [args]
```
```
$ dronecore mission { upload | download | set | } [args]
```
etc.

I shared this with @julianoes earlier. I just wanted to hear what is the feedback in the community.

Please share your thoughts.
Thanks.

title: Connect to serial and take_photo() returns TIMEOUT.
author: jean-dupond
body:
Hi everyone,

By running my code I intend to connect to the drone and simply take a photo triggering its pwm connected to the camera.

Code:

```
import asyncio

from mavsdk.camera import (CameraError, Mode)
from mavsdk import System


async def run():
    drone = System()
    await drone.connect(system_address="serial:///dev/ttyUSB0:57600")

    print("Waiting for drone to connect...")
    async for state in drone.core.connection_state():
        if state.is_connected:
            print(f"-- Connected to drone!")
            break
    
    print_mode_task = asyncio.ensure_future(print_mode(drone))
    print_status_task = asyncio.ensure_future(print_status(drone))
    running_tasks = [print_mode_task, print_status_task]
    
    print("Setting mode to 'PHOTO'")
    try:
        await drone.camera.set_mode(Mode.PHOTO)
    except CameraError as error:
        print(f"Setting mode failed with error code: {error._result.result}")
    
    
    print("Taking a photo")
    try:
        await drone.camera.take_photo()
    except CameraError as error:
        print(f"Couldn't take photo: {error._result.result}")


async def print_mode(drone):
    async for mode in drone.camera.mode():
        print(f"Camera mode: {mode}")


async def print_status(drone):
    async for status in drone.camera.status():
        print(status)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Run the asyncio loop
    asyncio.run(run())
```


It prints out a TIMEOUT result after the set_mode and take_photo were called...

The camera is properly plugged. I can trigger it by using **pymavlink** instead.

The reason I wanna use MAVSDK is the fact that I want to get back the CAMERA_IMAGE_CAPTURED information (lat,lon,etc.) and for that I need to use the command MAV_CMD_IMAGE_START_CAPTURE, which returns an UNSUPPORTED result when I send it from pymavlink... In [this post](https://discuss.px4.io/t/trigger-camera-from-onboard/16775/2) i saw that its because only MAVSDK supports it.

The only way i can trigger my camera now is using MAV_CMD_DO_SET_CAM_TRIGG_DIST from pymavlink, but like that i cannot get the CAMERA_IMAGE_CAPTURED info...

Can anyone tell me how to succeed? Either doing it from MAVSDK or pymavlink its okay for me.

Thanks in advance!

answer_comments.body:
Do you have a camera on the other side? Does it receive the command MAVSDK sends?

The timeout tells you that MAVSDK sent the command but did not receive an ACK. Can MAVSDK do other things with the drone, like arm/takeoff or list params?

> But the camera is not a mavlink camera.

Oh, I don't really know how the setup works then. But PX4 has to behave like the mavlink camera then, and it should trigger it itself, right?
Yes, PX4 would have to support https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_IMAGE_START_CAPTURE.
That API is not supported by PX4. You need a camera server that talks mavlink and can answer.

title: [Discussion] How to set a parameter and reboot the vehicle for PX4 MAVSDK SITL Test
author: junwoo091400
body:
## What I want to do
I wanted to have the following feature on [MAVSDK Test](https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/tree/main/test/mavsdk_tests) in PX4 SITL:
1. Set the parameter in PX4 (to set it to a non-default value)
2. Reboot the vehicle (Or start the vehicle directly with the modified parameter from the beginning)
3. Perform a SITL MAVSDK test with the vehicle that had the modified parameter when it booted up

The reason for this was for the [Payload delivery SITL test PR](https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/pull/20230), I needed a way to set the parameter and reboot the vehicle, in order to have the startup script recognize the non-default parameter to enable the `payload_deliverer` module, and start the module, which is necessary for payload delivery feature.

## Problem
Currently it seems like we can't arbitrarily set the parameter before booting up, neither can we reboot the vehicle in the SITL test function.

### Proposed Solutions
1. Have a way to reboot the vehicle after setting the parameter in the mavsdk sitl test pipeline
2. Have a way to load an arbitrary / modified parameter through MAVSDK interface for the drone

## Discussion 
If we want to support such feature, what would be the best way to implement it? Are there any other solutions? Would this be possible without modifying MAVSDK?

comments.body:
So the goal of the test is to check that the parameter is set correctly after reboot, but SITL resets the params when it boots, right?

I don't really see how this is related to MAVSDK, though :thinking:. It feels like you need SITL to persist the params (instead of resetting after reboot), and that's not how SITL does it, right?

1. From what I know there is not yet a way to reboot/restart PX4 from within PX4 in SITL but only externally via helper scripts. So for the PX4 mavsdk_tests you would have to script it there.
2. You can always load/get an arbitrary param from PX4. I think that part is not a problem.

Regarding your question: to me it sounds like a test script issue around PX4, and not a MAVSDK issue as such.

But then if it requires custom code to make it work in SITL, is it really a test? It feels like params persistence after reboot is just not a SITL feature. We can simulate it with external scripts, and then we can test that those external scripts simulate it correctly, but at the end of the day it's not testing the actual feature :sweat_smile:

I think I found the solution :thinking:, which is using a custom model with the airframe file specifying the parameters that needs to be changed on startup. It is of course not scalable, but for a SITL test for a specific feature, I think this can be tolerated.
